HeatScape / Center City, PhiladelphiaBuilt for the everyday walk.
HOW THIS MAP WORKS

Center City, Philadelphia

A working geometry and routing model, not a validated heat-navigation service.

Study area

Center City is the union of eight official neighborhood polygons from OpenDataPhilly: Center City East, Chinatown, Fitler Square, Logan Square, Old City, Rittenhouse, Society Hill and Washington Square West. Streets and buildings are included up to 150 m beyond that boundary so walks near the edge still route correctly.

Buildings and streets

Building footprints and walkable ways come from OpenStreetMap through the Overpass API. Heights use the OSM height tag, then floor count × 3.3 m, then an assumed 12 m (about 39 ft) where neither exists.

Tree canopy (LiDAR)

Crown outlines come from the city's 2015 Parks & Recreation canopy layer. Heights come from April 2022 classified LiDAR (NOAA dataset 9848): Python grids bare-earth returns at 2 m with rasterio, subtracts ground elevation from first returns inside each crown, screens out building roofs, and keeps the 90th-percentile height of at least five valid returns. Trees count in summer only; winter assumes leaf-off.

Sun and shade

SunCalc gives the sun position for the chosen date and time. Every building and crown is swept away from the sun by its height divided by the tangent of solar elevation (capped at 400 m). Each street segment is sampled every 10 m to find the share in shade. The time is held constant for the whole walk.

How routes are compared

Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest walk. Seven penalty weights on sun (summer) or shade (winter) produce alternatives. An alternative section replaces the matching part of the shortest walk only if it improves exposure and adds no more than the extra time you allow. This is a heuristic, not a guaranteed optimum.

Known gaps

Street centerlines stand in for sidewalks. Terrain, awnings, building relations in OSM, canopy change since the surveys, live closures, indoor routes and accessibility are not modeled.
